newsitem.title: UK: Oil refinery profits sink, Singapore still weak.
newsitem.headline: Oil refinery profits sink, Singapore still weak.

text.p: Profit margins at oil refineries fell last week as oil products failed to match gains on crude.
In Singapore and Europe the trend was steadily downward but in the United States profits picked up at the end of the week, according to calculations using standard yields of oil products.
In Singapore gasoline was hit hard, losing $1.74 a barrel against Dubai crude, while gas oil and heavy fuel were little changed against crude.
Complex margins ended the week at $2.36 a barrel an averaged $2.64 for the week. This was similar to the previous weeks but sharply below the April average of $5.31.
Simple margins were similarly weak, ending at 51 cents a barrel last Friday, which is sharply above negative values of a month ago but but well below spring levels of more than $3 a barrel.
Shell Singapore plans to maintain run cuts in July at its 435,000 barrels per day refinery, a company spokeswoman said on Friday.
The refinery's average runs in June were 58,000 tonnes per day (tpd), down from its normal capacity of 59,000 tpd, she said.
She added that the refinery had been targetting a June average of 57,000 tpd because of high stocks and weak margins.
"Directionally, the refinery will reduce its runs in July," she said. But she declined to give details about the July cut.
In Rotterdam complex refineries averaged $1.57 a barrel last week, compared to $2.30 the week before.
In the Mediterranean margins lost 86 cents a barrel to average $1.37 last week.
A complex refinery running Russian Urals has fallen steadily since a June 6 peak of $3.52 a barrel, ending last Friday at $1.04 a barrel.
On the U.S. Gulf coast profits running Brent averaged $1.08 a barrel last week, compared to $1.42 the week before.
Despite the weakness, profits picked up and ended at $1.26 on Friday as gasoline outstripped gains on Brent.
Unleaded gasoline on the U.S. Gulf coast ended some $5 a barrel above Brent on Friday compared to $4.90 the week before.
